Baby Tracker: Feeding, Sleep and Diaper Logs

Updated: September 26, 2026

Product guide by Mohammadamin Namyar, founder of BeMama.

BeMama’s baby tracker helps you record what happened, when it happened and which baby the entry belongs to. Use nursing and bottle feeding logs alongside sleep and diaper records, then review your entries in Reports. Here is how those app workflows differ from the free care tools on this website.

Start with the right baby profile

Sign in to the app and set up the baby journey with your child’s birth date. Open the baby tracking area and check the selected profile. Choose the type of entry you want to record; baby and older-child stages have different available actions.

Enter only the details you want to keep. Check the time and profile before saving, and use the entry’s edit controls if you need to correct a mistake.

Breastfeeding tracker: record a nursing session

Choose Nursing, select the starting side, then choose Timer for a session happening now or Manual for one that has already finished. For a manual entry, check the start and end time before saving. When using a timer, stop it when the session ends.

A nursing log records timing and side. Duration does not tell you how much milk your baby transferred, so the tracker cannot tell you whether a feed was sufficient.

Bottle feeding tracker: record milk type and amount

Choose Bottle and enter the feed time. Select breast milk or formula, choose mL or oz, and record the amount before saving. Check the unit when reviewing entries or changing devices.

Use the feeding tracker to remember amounts you recorded. It does not recommend a target intake or tell you how to prepare formula; follow the product instructions and your clinician’s advice.

Baby sleep tracker: save a sleep period

Choose Sleep to record a sleep period using the available start and end controls. For a running sleep timer, end it when your baby wakes. Review completed entries to see the timing of naps and overnight sleep.

The log depends on your entries. It does not automatically detect sleep, promise a next-nap time, or assess whether your baby is sleeping safely.

Diaper change tracker: record the change

Choose the diaper entry, select the relevant type and save the time. Together with nursing and bottle records, this gives you a feeding and diaper tracker in the same baby profile.

Review the entries when you need to recall a day’s care or prepare questions for an appointment. A diaper count alone cannot confirm hydration or rule out illness.

Review your day, week and recorded patterns

Open Reports for the selected child. Day, Week, List and Summary organize the records differently. The current CSV download covers that child’s latest 30 calendar days through today; check the saved file’s dates rather than assuming it follows the visible report filters.

Empty periods can mean nothing was logged, rather than no feeding or sleep happened. Report totals describe the entries you saved. They are not a diagnosis, a growth assessment or proof that a routine is working.

AI-assisted analysis and some advanced features have separate access requirements. See Free and Premium feature access

Free website tools: calculators, checklists and a growth log

The public tools at Free pregnancy and parenting tools work without an app account. They include ovulation and due date estimates, an appointment and symptom calendar, preparation checklists, a baby-name shortlist and a growth log.

Checklist tools let you add tasks and notes, filter the list, mark tasks done or not needed, review progress, and print or download a backup. The growth log plots your measurements and offers a WHO weight-for-age reference view for supported ages; it does not calculate an individual percentile.

These website tools save on the current device when you save your work. They do not automatically synchronize with the app. Clearing browser storage can remove saved work, so download backups you want to keep.

Read about account data and retention separately: Privacy, retention and export information

Shared care, both parents and twins

Keep a separate profile for each child, including twins. Check the selected name before starting a timer, adding a feed or opening Reports. At handover, compare the last saved event and any running timer so the next caregiver does not record the same activity twice.

Use separate caregiver accounts and confirm access to the intended child before relying on shared records. Access and management options depend on your account and app version; contact BeMama support if you cannot find them. Do not share your password. A record of who added an event helps explain a handover, but does not replace a conversation.

Where caregiver sharing is available, the profile owner invites a caregiver by email. The recipient must sign in with that same verified email to accept; invitations expire after seven days. Accepted caregivers have editor access. The owner controls pending invitations and caregiver removal. Confirm access on both accounts before handing over care.

Offline records and syncing between devices

Read the status on each care-history entry: Waiting to sync means the change is still local; Syncing means it is being sent; Synced confirms synchronization. Sync failed or Needs review calls for checking the entry rather than assuming it reached another device.

If a record is missing on another phone, first compare the account, child and event time. Reconnect the original phone and check its status. Keep the original local data until the issue is resolved; reinstalling is not a recovery step. If it still fails, send support the app version and error text, without private care notes.

Pumping tracker: total or left and right

Open the child’s care screen and choose Pumping. Under amount style, choose Total or Left / right, then select mL or oz. Use Timer for a session in progress or Manual for one you have finished. Check the start time and amount before saving.

For example, a left entry of 40 mL and a right entry of 30 mL describe one 70 mL pumping session. These are sample records, not a supply target. Do not also log the same session as a separate total. Open its care-history entry to correct it. A later bottle feed is a different event.

Read reports and export a useful care record

In Reports, confirm the child’s name in the heading. With multiple children, use the child-switch icon. Choose Day, Week, List or Summary for the question you want to answer, and check the dates and activity selection. Standard summaries and extended 90/365-day comparisons have different access requirements.

For CSV, use the download icon in Reports. The current app first tries to synchronize, then exports the selected child’s latest 30 calendar days through today. The on-screen date or activity filter does not redefine that export window. Choose a file destination and inspect the dates in the saved CSV before sharing it.

Example: two logged bottles of 60 mL and 90 mL total 150 mL of recorded bottle feeds. If another feed was not logged, that total is incomplete. Nursing duration is not milk volume. A blank period is missing information, not proof that nothing happened.

Growth records: read the measurements first

Choose Growth in the child’s care screen. Set the measurement date and units, then enter only the measurements you have: weight, length/height or head circumference. Leave unknown measurements blank. Save the entry and check it in care history; correct the original entry if its date or unit is wrong.

The screenshot shows measurement entry, not a clinical growth assessment. Read the child, date and unit together before comparing points. Basic care logging, the app’s separate Premium tools and the free browser growth log are different workflows.

Key takeaways

  • Choose the baby profile before recording a feed, sleep period or diaper change.
  • Nursing entries record timing and starting side; bottle entries record milk type, amount and unit.
  • Reports show saved records by day, week, list and summary, with a CSV download.
  • Missing entries are missing data, not evidence that no care happened.
  • Website tools and app tracking are separate; keep backups of records you need.

Frequently asked questions

Can BeMama track newborn feeding and diapers together?

Yes. A baby profile has nursing, bottle and diaper entries. Save each event with its time, then open Reports to review the records for that baby.

Can I use the app to track feedings when I breastfeed and bottle feed?

Yes. Use Nursing for sessions at the breast and Bottle for expressed milk or formula. Nursing time and bottle volume describe different things and should not be treated as equivalent intake measurements.

Does the baby sleep tracker predict the next nap?

This workflow records sleep entries and displays recorded patterns. It does not promise a next-nap prediction or a personalized sleep plan.

Will my website growth log appear in the app?

No. Website tools keep their own device-local records. Use the tool’s backup controls and enter information separately in the app if you want it there.

Is every tracking feature free?

Feature access can differ by account and platform. Daily Journey and the public website tools do not require an active Premium subscription, but check the app’s feature and subscription screens for advanced tools and AI access.

Why is a CSV different from the report I am viewing?

The export currently uses the selected child and a rolling 30-day window. The screen can show a different range or activity selection. Compare the dates and entries before drawing conclusions.

Can I fix a pumping entry without adding another session?

Yes. Open the saved entry in care history and edit it. Check the amount style, unit and time. Re-entering the same session as a new event can inflate recorded totals.

This article is general education, not medical advice, diagnosis, or treatment. Always talk with a qualified healthcare professional about your situation, and seek urgent care for emergencies.
